intro.text: **Please read carefully before using our services.**

Welcome to Stephen Corporate Services Ltd! SCS provides corporate, compliance and business operations support to businesses and professionals: commercial documentation coordination, HR and workforce administration, sales operations, customer support operations, regulatory and compliance coordination, and intellectual-property filing coordination (the “Services”). The Services are operated by **Stephen Corporate Services Ltd** (“we”, “us” or “SCS”) and are subject to these Terms of Service (“Terms”).

blocks.text: These Terms, the written service order for your engagement and any applicable schedule form a contract between you and SCS. You accept it by signing it, accepting a written proposal, paying an invoice after receiving these Terms, or instructing us to begin work. If you accept for an organisation, you confirm that you are authorised to do so. If you are under eighteen (18) years of age, you may not use the Services.

Mandatory law takes priority. A signed service order overrides these Terms only where it expressly names the term it changes. Part 2 (Data protection) governs personal data and takes priority over inconsistent wording on that subject. A service order cannot remove rights or duties imposed by law.

“Client” or “you” means the person or organisation purchasing the Services. “Services” means only the work stated in the accepted service order. “Deliverables” means the documents, reports, registers, training materials or other outputs expressly included in that order. “Client Data” means information, records and personal data supplied by or for you. “Authority” means a regulator, government agency, registry or other public body relevant to the Services. “Personal data” has the meaning given under applicable Nigerian data-protection law.

sections.heading: 4. Your service order defines what we do

blocks.text: We perform only the Services described in your accepted service order. Work outside that scope needs written agreement on the extra deliverables, fees and timing before it starts. Estimates and delivery dates depend on us receiving complete and accurate information, approvals and funds when required.

sections.heading: 5. We work with skill and care, but we do not guarantee outcomes

blocks.text: We perform our work with reasonable skill and care using suitable personnel. Unless a signed service order expressly says so, we do not guarantee any regulatory approval, licence, registration, sales result, revenue level, litigation outcome, tax result or commercial performance. Decisions and processing times of public authorities are outside our control.

We provide corporate services, administrative support, compliance coordination and business operations support within the agreed scope. Where a task legally requires a practising solicitor, licensed tax professional, accredited agent or other authorised professional, it will be handled by or referred to an appropriately qualified person. A solicitor-client relationship arises only where a practising legal practitioner expressly accepts a legal engagement. We do not represent ourselves as a licensed Data Protection Compliance Organisation (DPCO) unless we hold and confirm the relevant current licence.

sections.heading: 7. You must be truthful and cooperative

blocks.text: You must: (a) provide genuine, accurate and complete information; (b) disclose material changes promptly; (c) give timely instructions, approvals and access; (d) ensure you are entitled to provide any data or documents you supply; (e) make your own business decisions and meet your own statutory obligations; (f) review drafts and deliverables before use or filing; (g) pay invoices and third-party costs on time; and (h) not ask us to make a false, misleading or unlawful filing or statement.

sections.heading: 8. Our fees are those in your service order

blocks.text: Unless stated otherwise, fees are in Nigerian naira and exclude VAT and other applicable taxes, which we show on our invoice. Official filing fees, registry charges, courier fees and charges of external professionals are separate costs and may be required in advance. We will obtain your approval before incurring a material unlisted third-party expense.

Invoices are payable within ten (10) calendar days of issue unless the service order states a different period. If an invoice is overdue, we may give written notice and suspend work if payment remains outstanding after a reasonable opportunity to remedy the default. We may withhold unpaid, non-essential deliverables to the extent lawful, but we will not use an unpaid invoice to unlawfully keep personal data or block a legally required data return. Late-payment interest applies only if your service order states it; no unstated rate applies.

sections.heading: 10. Government and third-party fees follow their own rules

blocks.text: Amounts paid to a public authority or external provider are subject to that recipient’s rules and refund policy. We will pass on receipts or payment evidence we receive. We are not responsible for an authority’s delay, rejection or decision, except to the extent directly caused by our own failure to perform an agreed task with reasonable care.

Each party must protect the other’s non-public business, financial, technical and commercial information, use it only for the agreement, and share it only with personnel or advisers who need it and are bound by confidentiality duties. This does not apply to information that is public without breach, already lawfully known, independently developed or lawfully received from another source. A party may disclose information where law or a competent authority requires it, giving advance notice where legally permitted. Confidentiality obligations continue for five (5) years after the agreement ends; personal-data obligations continue for as long as the data is held.

Each party keeps the rights in materials it owned or developed independently before the engagement. You keep your brands, records and information. After full payment, you own bespoke documents prepared specifically for you, excluding our pre-existing templates, methods, know-how and reusable materials embedded in them. We grant you a non-exclusive licence to use those embedded materials as part of the deliverable for your own business. You may not resell our templates or use them to build a competing template or compliance service without written permission. We will not use your name or logo in publicity without your written consent.

We may use suitably qualified employees, contractors or service providers and remain responsible for our own contractual obligations. If you separately appoint an external professional, that professional is responsible for their own advice and work under their separate engagement. We will disclose material third-party involvement where it matters to scope, confidentiality or the handling of personal data.

sections.heading: 14. You must review what we deliver

blocks.text: You are responsible for checking that names, dates, corporate details, amounts and other facts are correct before signing, filing or relying on any deliverable. Unless your service order says so, we are not engaged to audit your records, verify every underlying fact or monitor legal changes after delivery.

sections.heading: 15. Lawful use only, and we may pause or refuse unlawful instructions

blocks.text: We apply a strict policy against money laundering, terrorism financing, bribery, corruption and dealings with sanctioned persons or territories. You must not use the Services or any SCS website or platform to: break any law; submit false, misleading or forged information or documents; attempt unauthorised access, interfere with security or introduce malicious code; scrape or unlawfully collect others’ personal data; or infringe anyone’s intellectual-property rights. We may pause or decline work, with an explanation where lawful and practicable, if we reasonably believe an instruction is unlawful, information may be forged or misleading, necessary information has not been supplied, payment is overdue after notice, or continuing would breach a legal or professional obligation. Where the law requires, we may report suspected unlawful conduct to the relevant authorities.

Each party is responsible for loss caused by its own breach of the agreement, negligence, fraud or wilful misconduct, subject to applicable law. Neither party is liable for indirect or consequential loss, loss of anticipated profit or loss of opportunity, except where the law does not permit the exclusion or the loss arises from fraud, wilful misconduct, confidentiality breach or a matter that cannot lawfully be excluded. Our total liability for a service order is limited to the professional fees paid or payable for that service order in the twelve (12) months before the event giving rise to the claim. This limit does not apply to liability that cannot legally be limited, and it does not limit a data subject’s statutory rights, regulatory powers or a party’s statutory data-protection obligations.

A party that causes a third-party claim or loss through its breach, unlawful conduct, fraud or negligent act must bear the portion of the loss fairly attributable to it, subject to applicable law. A party seeking recovery must notify the other promptly, cooperate reasonably and take reasonable steps to reduce the loss. No party may settle a claim in a way that imposes an admission or obligation on the other without that party’s written consent, which must not be unreasonably withheld.

The agreement begins when the first service order is accepted and continues until all services under it are completed or terminated. A recurring service renews only if the service order expressly provides for renewal; otherwise it ends at the stated end date. Where a recurring service renews, either party may prevent renewal by giving thirty (30) days’ written notice before the renewal date.

Either party may terminate a service order for material breach if the other fails to remedy it within fourteen (14) days after written notice. Either party may terminate where performance becomes unlawful or the other becomes insolvent or ceases business. Either party may end a recurring service for convenience on thirty (30) days’ written notice unless the service order provides otherwise. We may suspend or terminate immediately where necessary to comply with law or to guard against a credible unlawful instruction.

sections.heading: 20. What happens when a service ends

blocks.text: You pay for work performed up to the termination date and approved non-cancellable third-party costs. We refund any advance fee for work not performed, less amounts properly due. Within thirty (30) days after termination we give you the completed, paid-for deliverables and reasonable handover materials. Personal data is returned or deleted as set out in clause 22. We may keep the minimum records required by law or reasonably needed to establish, exercise or defend legal claims, with appropriate protection and retention limits.

Neither party is liable for delay caused by events reasonably beyond its control, such as natural disaster, major network or power outage, civil emergency or government action, provided it informs the other party and takes reasonable steps to resume performance. This does not excuse payment already due, confidentiality, reasonable security measures or legally required breach notifications. If the event prevents substantial performance for more than sixty (60) consecutive days, either party may terminate the affected service order by written notice.

This clause applies whenever we handle personal data in connection with a service. The parties must apply the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, the Nigeria Data Protection Commission’s applicable directives and other applicable law. These terms describe operational responsibilities; they do not make either party compliant merely by being signed.

items: **22.1 Roles.** For personal data we handle only to provide your service, such as your customer, employee, applicant, supplier or contact records, you normally decide the purpose and act as controller, and we act as processor. We act as controller for our own business records, including client contacts, billing, fraud prevention, recruitment, our own staff, legal records and any marketing we independently decide to conduct. Actual roles depend on who determines the purpose and essential means of the processing, not on the label used.

**22.2 Instructions and permitted use.** As processor, we process personal data only for the service purpose and on your documented instructions unless law requires otherwise. We will tell you if we reasonably believe an instruction breaches data-protection law, unless law prohibits that notice. We will not sell your personal data or use it to train a general-purpose artificial-intelligence model. Any new use, purpose or materially different technology must be assessed and agreed in writing first.

**22.3 Your responsibilities as controller.** You must identify and document a lawful basis for each purpose; give people a clear privacy notice when required; collect only data reasonably needed; ensure the data you give us was lawfully obtained; respond to data-subject requests; assess whether a privacy impact assessment is needed; and make required notifications or filings. Do not send us personal data that is unnecessary for the agreed service.

**22.4 Confidentiality and personnel.** We ensure people authorised to handle personal data are bound by appropriate confidentiality obligations and receive role-relevant guidance. Access is limited to personnel who need it. You must likewise restrict access to SCS-provided credentials and personal data.

**22.5 Security.** Each party must maintain security measures appropriate to the sensitivity and volume of the data, the risks to individuals and the nature of the processing. Depending on the service, safeguards should include unique user accounts, strong authentication, least-privilege access, secure transmission, encryption where appropriate, device and software updates, malware protection, secure backups, access logging, physical security for paper records, staff awareness and a documented response process. Neither party should claim a safeguard is in place unless it has been implemented.

**22.6 Incidents.** A party that becomes aware of a suspected or confirmed incident affecting personal data handled under the service must notify the other without undue delay and provide the information reasonably available. We will help you, within the agreed scope, with containment, investigation and records. The controller remains responsible for deciding and making the regulatory and individual notifications the law requires, unless the parties agree otherwise in writing or the law places the duty directly on us. Each party must preserve relevant evidence and document the incident and corrective action.

**22.7 Requests from individuals.** If we receive a request about data we process for you, we will forward it to you without undue delay and assist reasonably. We will not decide your response unless legally required or authorised. For data we control ourselves, requests may be sent to {{email_privacy}}, and we will respond within the time applicable law requires, subject to lawful extensions or exceptions.

**22.8 Minimisation, accuracy and retention.** Each party must limit collection and access to what is reasonably necessary, correct inaccurate information when notified, and keep personal data only as long as needed for the stated purpose or a lawful retention requirement. At the end of a service we return or securely delete your personal data on your documented choice, unless law or a legitimate legal-claims need requires limited retention. Retained data stays protected and must be deleted when the reason ends. Any service-specific retention period should be recorded in the service order.

**22.9 Subcontractors and technology providers.** We use a subcontractor or technology provider only where reasonably necessary for the service and subject to appropriate confidentiality, security and data-protection obligations. Where the law requires, we give you advance notice of a material change in subprocessors and a reasonable opportunity to raise a substantiated data-protection objection. We remain responsible for our own contractual obligations regarding our subprocessors. Do not assume that a particular provider, platform or hosting country is used unless confirmed in the service order or written data-processing particulars.

**22.10 International transfers.** Neither party may transfer personal data outside Nigeria in connection with the service unless the transfer meets applicable Nigerian data-protection law, including any adequacy, safeguard, permitted-derogation or regulatory-approval requirements. Before a transfer, the responsible party must identify the recipient, destination, purpose and lawful mechanism, assess the risks and give the other party any required information. Consent is not a default workaround for an otherwise non-compliant transfer.

**22.11 Sensitive data and children.** You must identify sensitive personal data before sending it to us and explain why it is needed. The specific legal conditions and heightened safeguards for such data apply. Data about children or persons who need additional protection must not be collected or processed unless the service requires it and the applicable conditions, notices, authorisations and safeguards have been addressed.

**22.12 Impact assessments and new technology.** Before processing likely to create a high risk to people, the party responsible for deciding the processing must assess whether a data protection impact assessment is required and complete it where required. We provide reasonable information about our part of the service. New profiling, systematic monitoring, biometric processing, large-scale sensitive-data use, automated decisions or AI-enabled processing must not be introduced casually; the parties must first assess necessity, fairness, transparency, human oversight, security and legal requirements.

**22.13 Evidence and audits.** On reasonable written request, each party provides information reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance with this clause, subject to confidentiality, security and legal restrictions. Audits must be proportionate, scheduled in normal business hours, protect other clients’ information and avoid unreasonable disruption. A reasonable alternative, such as policy extracts, an independent assessment summary or evidence of required filings, may be used where it adequately addresses the request. A serious incident, a regulator’s lawful request or credible evidence of material non-compliance may justify an earlier review.

**22.14 Regulatory status.** Each party decides whether it must register with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, file a compliance audit return, appoint a data protection officer or meet other requirements for its own activities. We will not say that we or you are registered, audited, certified or licensed unless that status has been verified. Where a task legally requires a licensed DPCO or another authorised professional, the parties must arrange for that qualified provider to do it.

**22.15 Return and deletion at exit.** At the end of the service, on your reasonable written request, we return your personal data in a commonly used format where reasonably practicable, or securely delete it, and take reasonable steps to instruct relevant subprocessors to do the same. Records we must keep by law or for a legal claim are restricted and limited to what is necessary. Backups may remain until overwritten in the ordinary secure backup cycle, provided they are protected and not restored or used except for recovery or legal compliance.

**22.16 Statutory responsibility stays where the law puts it.** The agreement allocates tasks between the parties but does not remove duties the law imposes directly on either of them. Each party remains responsible for its own conduct, regulatory obligations and response to a regulator. Nothing here limits an individual’s rights or a competent authority’s powers.

sections.heading: Part 3: Disputes, notices and general terms

blocks.text: The agreement is governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. The parties will first try in good faith to resolve a dispute through discussions between authorised representatives. If there is no resolution within thirty (30) days after written notice of the dispute, either party may pursue mediation or proceedings before a court of competent jurisdiction in Nigeria. Arbitration applies only where the parties separately agree in writing on the procedure and appointment mechanism. Nothing in this clause limits a person’s right to complain to the Nigeria Data Protection Commission or to seek any remedy the law provides.

Formal notices must be sent by email or delivered to the contact details in the service order or the company details above. An email notice is treated as received on the next business day if no delivery failure is received. A party must promptly tell the other of any change in its notice details.

Any SCS website or platform must be used lawfully. Website content is general information unless expressly stated otherwise in a signed engagement. Electronic signatures and signed copies exchanged electronically may be used to the extent permitted by Nigerian law.

The agreement is the entire agreement for the Services and replaces earlier discussions on the same subject, except for liability for fraud. Changes must be agreed in writing; we may update these website Terms for future engagements by posting them with at least thirty (30) days’ notice, but an update does not change a service order already accepted unless you agree. Failing to enforce a right is not a waiver. Neither party may assign the agreement without the other’s consent, except that we may assign it to a successor to substantially all of our business if the successor assumes the relevant obligations. If a term is unenforceable, the remaining terms continue. The parties are independent contractors; the agreement creates no employment, partnership or joint venture. Neither party may offer or accept an improper payment in connection with the Services.
